AI.method: Combines early-time optical photometry and spectroscopy of 27 previously unpublished SNe II from the POISE collaboration with 59 literature events (86 total), providing near-daily cadence, percent-level precision uBgVri light curves. SNe are classified as flash or non-flash based on spectra within four days of explosion. Key photometric properties—rise times, peak absolute magnitudes, color evolution—are measured and compared between classes.
AI.result: Flash SNe are on average more luminous at peak and generally bluer than non-flash events, with distinct color distributions at 20 days post-explosion (likely intrinsic rather than extinction-driven). Statistically significant differences appear in B-band rise times, with flash SNe showing a tail toward longer rise times. Color-curve breaks within 30 days, combined with the slope change across the break and absolute peak magnitude, provide a strong diagnostic of flash spectroscopic properties.
AI.conclusion: Photometric observations alone—specifically color-curve breaks within 30 days together with peak magnitude and pre/post-break slopes—can identify SNe II interacting with dense circumstellar material, even without early-time spectroscopy.

title: Relations between optical spectral parameters and the (far-)infrared continuum in Type~1 active galactic nuclei
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: This study combines multi-wavelength continuum data with optical spectral properties for a far-infrared (FIR)-selected sample of Type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGNs) from AKARI data. We explore the relation between AGN physics and concomitant star formation processes using empirical correlations of optical and multiwavelength data. We measured spectral parameters including full widths at half maximum (FWHMs) and velocity shifts of broad and narrow optical emission lines, as well as continuum luminosities from GALEX FUV to AKARI 160 microns. The sample contains 88 AGNs observed at both optical and FIR wavelengths. About 50% are Seyfert 1s with both broad H$β$ and H$α$ lines; almost all remaining objects are S1.9s with only broad H$α$. The FWHMs of broad H$β$ and H$α$ are anti-correlated with luminosity in most bands. Shifts of narrow H$β$, H$α$, and [O III] 5007 lines and FWHM of [O III] 5007 correlate with optical and IR luminosities. Luminosities at 65 and 90 microns are more strongly connected with optical and other spectral properties than those at 140 and 160 microns. These trends extend the well-known Eigenvector 1 (EV1) correlations into the MIR and FIR domain. The anti-correlation between broad-line FWHMs and NIR and MIR luminosities is probably caused by the inclination of the torus and accretion disc: higher inclinations see less AGN radiation. However, most objects fall into Population A along the quasar EV1 main sequence, where narrower broad H$β$ profiles and FIR excess emission are commonly linked to higher Eddington ratios.

AI.tldr: This study links optical spectral parameters of 88 AKARI-selected FIR Type 1 AGNs to multi-wavelength continuum luminosities, finding that broad-/narrow-line width and shift correlations extend the Eigenvector 1 sequence into the mid- and far-infrared, likely driven jointly by torus/disc inclination and Eddington ratio.
AI.motivation: The physical connection between AGN activity and coeval star formation, and how the well-known Eigenvector 1 (EV1) correlations behave outside the optical/UV regime, remain unclear—particularly for FIR-selected Type 1 AGNs where the dusty torus and host star formation dominate the IR emission.
AI.method: Combined multi-wavelength continuum photometry (GALEX FUV through AKARI 160 μm) with optical spectroscopy for a FIR-selected sample of 88 Type 1 AGNs. Measured FWHMs and velocity shifts of broad and narrow Hβ, Hα, and [O III] 5007, then tested empirical correlations of these spectral parameters against continuum luminosities across bands.
AI.result: Roughly 50% are Seyfert 1s with both broad Hβ and Hα; nearly all remaining objects are S1.9s with broad Hα only. Broad Hβ and Hα FWHMs anti-correlate with luminosity in most bands. Narrow Hβ, Hα, and [O III] 5007 shifts, plus [O III] 5007 FWHM, correlate with optical and IR luminosities. Luminosities at 65 and 90 μm track optical/spectral properties more strongly than those at 140 and 160 μm.
AI.conclusion: The observed trends extend EV1 correlations into the MIR/FIR domain. The broad-line FWHM–NIR/MIR luminosity anti-correlation is plausibly caused by torus and accretion-disc inclination, while most objects lie in Population A of the quasar EV1 main sequence, where narrower broad Hβ and FIR excess are commonly associated with higher Eddington ratios.

title: The coordinated radio and infrared survey for high-mass star formation - VI. Higher-resolution follow-up of point-like northern ultra-compact H II regions
comment: 24 pages, 12 figures
summary: The CORNISH survey provided the most complete sample of ultra-compact H II (UCHII) regions in the northern Galactic plane to date, but at its 1.5 arcsec resolution the most compact, and plausibly youngest, members of the sample could not be morphologically classified. We present Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (JVLA) A-configuration observations at 10 GHz of 69 such CORNISH UCHII regions, reaching an angular resolution of ~0.2-0.3 arcsec and a typical rms noise of ~10 microJy/beam. All but two of the imaged targets are detected; the two non-detections lie in fields that are dynamic-range limited by bright neighbours. Six targets (~9 per cent) are resolved into pairs of sources, and a further 15 CORNISH UCHII regions detected within the fields reveal complex, multi-component structure. We also report candidate massive young stellar object (MYSO) jet knots and a row of three compact sources coincident with a previously unresolved infrared-dark H II region. The targets have a median deconvolved angular diameter of ~0.9 arcsec and physical diameters of 0.004-0.17 pc (median ~0.03 pc), with no correlation between angular size and distance, consistent with a population of intrinsically compact, young regions. Spectral indices between 1.4 and 10 GHz place ~32 per cent of the targets below the thermal free-free limit, possibly indicating non-thermal emission or variability. These data enable morphological classification of nearly the entire CORNISH UCHII sample, which will be presented in a forthcoming paper.

AI.tldr: JVLA A-configuration 10 GHz observations resolve 69 of the most compact CORNISH UCHII regions at ~0.2-0.3 arcsec, revealing median deconvolved diameters of ~0.9 arcsec (~0.03 pc) and complex sub-structure, completing morphological classification of the sample.
AI.motivation: The CORNISH survey gave the most complete sample of ultra-compact H II regions in the northern Galactic plane, but at 1.5 arcsec resolution the most compact and plausibly youngest members could not be morphologically classified. Higher angular resolution was needed to characterize these sources.
AI.method: JVLA A-configuration observations at 10 GHz of 69 compact CORNISH UCHII regions, achieving ~0.2-0.3 arcsec angular resolution and ~10 microJy/beam typical rms noise; multiwavelength spectral indices between 1.4 and 10 GHz were derived.
AI.result: All but two targets detected (the two non-detections lie in dynamic-range-limited fields near bright neighbours). Six targets (~9 per cent) resolved into pairs, and 15 further CORNISH UCHII regions in the fields show complex multi-component structure; candidate MYSO jet knots and three compact sources coincident with a previously unresolved infrared-dark H II region are reported. Median deconvolved diameter is ~0.9 arcsec, with physical diameters 0.004-0.17 pc (median ~0.03 pc) and no size-distance correlation, consistent with intrinsically compact young regions. About 32 per cent of targets fall below the thermal free-free limit between 1.4 and 10 GHz, possibly indicating non-thermal emission or variability.
AI.conclusion: These observations enable morphological classification of nearly the entire CORNISH UCHII sample, which will be presented in a forthcoming paper.

title: Milky Way Near Twins (MWNeTs). II. Applications of a Hierarchical Framework to NGC 3521, NGC 2903, UGC 11487, and CGCG 047-026
comment: 20 pages, 9 figures, 3 Tables, submitted to A&A
summary: Galaxies resembling the Milky Way in present-day global properties may have followed different evolutionary histories. The Milky Way Near Twins (MWNeT) framework introduced in Paper~I addresses this through seven successive stages of present-day compatibility and evolutionary diagnostics. We apply this framework to NGC~3521, NGC~2903, UGC~11487, and CGCG~047-026, spanning different levels of observational completeness and outcomes within the hierarchy. We combine archival measurements with analyses of galaxy structure, spectral-energy-distribution similarity, atomic-gas profiles, and optical nuclear diagnostics. Stages~I--IV assess environmental, structural, nuclear, and global compatibility; Stages~V--VII examine SEDs, rotation curves, and evolutionary fingerprints. We distinguish supported compatibility, partial agreement, measured incompatibility, and unconstrained diagnostics. We jointly assess these four galaxies within the MWNeT framework for the first time and derive new structural, SED-comparison, and H\,{\sc i} profile measurements for UGC~11487. NGC~2903 is a well-constrained benchmark, whereas NGC~3521 combines extensive evolutionary information with uncertain bar identification. UGC~11487 has a securely detected bar, quantitative UV--IR SED similarity, and distinctive transient nuclear tracers, but its nominal stellar mass lies below the adopted interval and its extended rotation curve remains unconstrained. CGCG~047-026 meets the initial environmental, structural, and nuclear-state criteria but remains largely unconstrained at higher stages. The four applications demonstrate the framework's ability to organise complementary evidence and identify observational priorities without equating missing data with physical incompatibility. They establish a basis for future systematic searches and for using candidate near twins as external laboratories of Milky Way evolution.

AI.tldr: The paper applies the 7-stage Milky Way Near Twins (MWNeT) framework to four candidate galaxies (NGC 3521, NGC 2903, UGC 11487, CGCG 047-026), organizing multi-wavelength evidence into supported, partial, incompatible, or unconstrained diagnostics to identify observational priorities.
AI.motivation: Galaxies that resemble the Milky Way today may have evolved very differently, so present-day similarity alone is insufficient to identify genuine "near twins." Paper I introduced the MWNeT framework to jointly assess present-day compatibility and evolutionary diagnostics; this work tests and demonstrates it on real galaxies.
AI.method: Combines archival data with new analyses of structure, SED similarity, atomic-gas (H I) profiles, and optical nuclear diagnostics. Stages I–IV check environmental, structural, nuclear, and global compatibility; Stages V–VII examine SEDs, rotation curves, and evolutionary fingerprints. Results are tagged as supported compatibility, partial agreement, measured incompatibility, or unconstrained.
AI.result: NGC 2903 is a well-constrained benchmark; NGC 3521 has rich evolutionary information but ambiguous bar identification; UGC 11487 has a secure bar, quantitative UV–IR SED similarity, and distinctive transient nuclear tracers, yet its stellar mass is below the adopted range and its extended rotation curve is unconstrained; CGCG 047-026 passes early criteria but is largely unconstrained at higher stages. New structural, SED-comparison, and H I measurements are reported for UGC 11487.
AI.conclusion: The four applications show the framework organizes complementary evidence and prioritizes observations without conflating missing data with physical incompatibility, providing a basis for systematic near-twin searches and using candidates as external laboratories of Milky Way evolution.

title: Inferring the delay time distribution of type Ia supernovae with CAALAM I: SED modelling choices and their effect on the delay time distribution
comment: 16 pages, 18 figures, Submitting to A&A
summary: A delay time distribution (DTD) quantifies the lag between progenitor formation and the subsequent explosive event. The DTD for a sample of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) from a survey can be modelled through relative rates and the star formation histories (SFH) of all individual galaxies. Modern wide-field surveys require computationally efficient methods to model the DTD without modelling large samples of non-host galaxies. We model the DTD for a volume limited sample from SNe Ia from the Zwicky Transient Facility. The aim is to study the effect of varying SED modelling assumptions, including stellar templates, dust attenuation, SFH models, and photometric coverage. We present a new modelling framework, the Conditional Astral Ancestry Latency Analysis Machine (CAALAM), to infer the DTD of a sample of SNe Ia from the posterior of their host galaxy SFH. A model consisting of a standard stellar template, a non-parametric SFH and a flexible dust attenuation law, is favoured by the data and predicts a non-parametric DTD peaking at 100-330 Myr. When modelled as a power law, the DTD has a characteristic exponent of $-1.30 \pm 0.04$. The exponent is sensitive to dust attenuation, photometry, or SFH. When the DTD is convolved with the SFHs of the host galaxies, we find a bimodal progenitor age distribution, with $\sim60\%$ of progenitors with ages around 1.1-3.6 Gyr and the remaining progenitors older than 3.6 Gyr. We show a correspondence between the modes of the distributions of SN Ia light curve stretch and the progenitor ages. Our inferred DTD implies that most SNe Ia ($\sim 60\%$) occur promptly within 330 Myr of progenitor formation. However, the implied progenitor ages from the DTD convolved with the SFHs from our sample are significantly older. This suggests that the DTD might be a mixture of a prompt and an extended progenitor channel.

AI.tldr: The authors introduce CAALAM, a computationally efficient framework that infers the delay time distribution (DTD) of SNe Ia from host-galaxy SFH posteriors, and apply it to a ZTF volume-limited sample, finding a non-parametric DTD peaking at 100-330 Myr and a power-law exponent of -1.30 ± 0.04.
AI.motivation: A DTD links progenitor formation to explosion, but modern wide-field surveys make it impractical to model large samples of non-host galaxies; efficient methods that exploit host-galaxy SFH posteriors are needed. The study also aims to quantify how SED-modelling choices (stellar templates, dust attenuation, SFH models, photometric coverage) propagate into the inferred DTD.
AI.method: Developed the Conditional Astral Ancestry Latency Analysis Machine (CAALAM), a new modelling framework that infers the DTD of a SNe Ia sample from the posterior SFHs of their host galaxies, avoiding modelling non-host galaxies. Applied to a volume-limited ZTF SNe Ia sample, testing combinations of stellar templates, parametric vs. non-parametric SFH, dust attenuation laws and photometric coverage.
AI.result: A model with a standard stellar template, non-parametric SFH and flexible dust attenuation law is favoured. The non-parametric DTD peaks at 100-330 Myr; as a power law it has exponent -1.30 ± 0.04, sensitive to dust attenuation, photometry and SFH assumptions. Convolving the DTD with host SFHs yields a bimodal progenitor age distribution: ~60% at 1.1-3.6 Gyr and the remainder older than 3.6 Gyr. Modes of the SN Ia light-curve stretch distribution correspond to the progenitor-age modes.
AI.conclusion: Although ~60% of SNe Ia occur promptly (within 330 Myr of progenitor formation), the progenitor ages implied by convolving the DTD with the sample's SFHs are significantly older, indicating that the DTD is likely a mixture of a prompt and an extended progenitor channel.

title: Comparing Infrared & X-ray-selected Active Galactic Nuclei host galaxy star formation rates to the galaxy main sequence
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: A key method of exploring the relationship between active galactic nuclei (AGN) and their host galaxies is to determine the astrophysical properties of galaxies that host AGN, and compare them to those that do not. Star formation rates are believed to be strongly related to nuclear activity, both indirectly via their common fuel supply, and directly via the energy injected by the AGN either suppressing or enhancing star formation. Strong observational evidence of a direct link between nuclear activity and in-situ star formation has proven elusive, likely in part due to the very different timescales of nuclear activity and episodes of star formation. To overcome these challenges, some studies have demonstrated that evidence of the aforementioned link may be found in the distributions of AGN power and star formation rates. While previous attempts to determine these distributions have largely focused on X-ray-selected samples of AGN, in this study we also attempt to determine the star formation rate distributions of infrared-selected AGN. The results vary between our samples, but at low redshift (0.8 < z < 1.2) we find that more powerful X-ray-selected AGN are more likely to occur in galaxies with higher specific star formation rates, consistent with previous studies. At higher redshifts (1.0 < z < 1.8), this trend is reversed with higher power AGN tending to occur in galaxies with lower specific star formation rates. By contrast, infrared-selected galaxies at 1.0 < z < 1.8 show no evidence of a changing star formation rate distribution with AGN power.

AI.tldr: This study compares star formation rate (SFR) distributions of X-ray- and infrared-selected AGN hosts across redshift, finding that X-ray AGN power correlates with higher specific SFR at low z but lower specific SFR at higher z, while IR-selected AGN show no such dependence.
AI.motivation: AGN and host-galaxy star formation are thought to be linked through a shared fuel supply and through AGN feedback (suppression or enhancement), but direct observational evidence is elusive, likely because nuclear activity and star formation operate on very different timescales. Examining the distributions of AGN power and SFR has been proposed as a way to circumvent these timescale mismatches.
AI.method: The authors determine SFR distributions for AGN host galaxies, extending prior work—which focused largely on X-ray-selected AGN samples—by also deriving SFR distributions for infrared-selected AGN. They then test whether these distributions vary with AGN power across different redshift bins.
AI.result: Results differ between samples. At low redshift (0.8 < z < 1.2), more powerful X-ray-selected AGN preferentially reside in galaxies with higher specific SFR, consistent with earlier studies. At higher redshift (1.0 < z < 1.8), the trend reverses: higher-power AGN tend to occur in galaxies with lower specific SFR. In contrast, infrared-selected galaxies at 1.0 < z < 1.8 show no evidence of a changing SFR distribution with AGN power.
AI.conclusion: The AGN–star formation connection inferred from SFR distributions is sample-dependent and redshift-dependent: X-ray-selected AGN exhibit a redshift-evolving relation between AGN power and specific SFR, whereas IR-selected AGN show none, underscoring the importance of selection wavelength in interpreting AGN–host co-evolution.

title: Broad Line Regions behind a Haze II: A Three-dimensional Electron-scattering Model of the Broad Br$γ$ Line in NGC 3783
comment: 24 pages, 7 figures, accepted by ApJ
summary: We investigate the broad Br$γ$ line in the type-1 active galactic nucleus NGC 3783 using three-dimensional Monte Carlo electron-scattering radiative transfer with SKIRT. Paper-I reproduced the observed smooth core and broad wings by convolving an intrinsic Keplerian profile with the analytic electron-scattering kernel of Laor (2006). Here we instead transport photons through explicit source and scattering geometries. For a partially covered Keplerian source, three-dimensional transfer broadens only the scattered photons and leaves an unscattered double-peaked core. For the thin Keplerian source motivated by Paper-I, a comparison of four scattering-geometry classes shows that neither a disk-like scatterer nor the tested halo variants reproduce both the core and wings. We therefore construct a two-component-source (2CS) model containing an inner Keplerian source disk, a rotating disk haze, a nearly spherical halo haze, and direct emission from a slower outer disk. A reference 2CS calculation gives Xi^2 =1.154 at i=15 deg. Polar cones with an input radial optical depth tau_hole=0.1 preserve the line profile and give a measured Thomson-thin sightline. The preferred low redistribution width, full-column ionization, and weak recombination emission cannot all be realized by a uniform thermal halo. The 2CS model is therefore a physically motivated parametric description whose medium must ultimately be tested with self-consistent radiative transfer, ionization, and dynamics.

AI.tldr: The authors model the broad Br$\gamma$ line of NGC 3783 with 3D Monte Carlo electron-scattering radiative transfer (SKIRT), showing that single-geometry scatterers fail to reproduce both the line core and wings, and propose a two-component-source model that fits the profile reasonably well ($\chi^2=1.154$ at $i=15^\circ$).
AI.motivation: Paper-I reproduced the smooth core and broad wings of the Br$\gamma$ line via analytic convolution of a Keplerian profile with an electron-scattering kernel. This work aims to move beyond that analytic approach by explicitly transporting photons through physical source and scattering geometries in 3D.
AI.method: 3D Monte Carlo electron-scattering radiative transfer with SKIRT applied to the type-1 AGN NGC 3783. The authors test a partially covered Keplerian source and four scattering-geometry classes (disk-like and halo variants) against a thin Keplerian source, then build a two-component-source (2CS) model consisting of an inner Keplerian disk, a rotating disk haze, a nearly spherical halo haze, and direct emission from a slower outer disk. Polar cones with radial optical depth $\tau_{\rm hole}=0.1$ are also examined.
AI.result: For a partially covered Keplerian source, 3D transfer broadens only scattered photons, leaving an unscattered double-peaked core. For the thin Keplerian source, neither a disk-like scatterer nor the tested halo variants reproduce both core and wings. The 2CS model yields $\chi^2=1.154$ at $i=15^\circ$; polar cones with $\tau_{\rm hole}=0.1$ preserve the line profile and give a Thomson-thin measured sightline.
AI.conclusion: The preferred narrow redistribution width, full-column ionization, and weak recombination emission cannot all be realized by a uniform thermal halo. The 2CS model is thus a physically motivated parametric description whose scattering medium must ultimately be validated with self-consistent radiative transfer, ionization, and dynamics.

title: Isomer-resolved ion-molecule reaction kinetics of HCO+ and HOC+
comment: accepted in A&A
summary: The HCO$^+$/HOC$^+$ abundance ratio has been observed to vary significantly in different astrophysical environments, making it an important diagnostic tool for exploring the interstellar medium. However, uncertainties in the reaction rates and branching ratios of key chemical reactions involving these ions affect the conclusions drawn from observations of either these species or other species that are derived on their basis. Here, we present isomer-resolved ion-molecule reaction rate coefficients of reactions involving HCO$^+$ and HOC$^+$ using a cryogenic ion trap experiment. We measured the rate coefficients of the isomerization reaction of HOC$^+$ to HCO$^+$ with H$_2$ and CO, as well as three different reactions producing both isomers: CO$^+$ + H$_2$ , H$_3^+$ + CO, and ArH$^+$ + CO. Our results show that the reaction of CO$^+$ with H$_2$ predominantly produces HCO$^+$ with a negligible yield of HOC$^+$ . This result is in agreement with recent theoretical predictions, but in major contrast to the generally accepted branching ratio based on previous experimental results. We also find that the isomerization reaction of HOC$^+$ to HCO$^+$ is efficient with both H2 and CO. We were able to assess the impact of our new measured reaction rate coefficients on the predicted HCO$^+$/HOC$^+$ abundance ratio using a state-of-the-art astrochemical model.

AI.tldr: Isomer-resolved cryogenic ion trap measurements revise key reaction rate coefficients and branching ratios for HCO+/HOC+, notably showing CO+ + H2 produces almost exclusively HCO+, and that HOC+ isomerization with H2 and CO is efficient, altering astrochemical predictions of the HCO+/HOC+ ratio.
AI.motivation: The HCO+/HOC+ abundance ratio is a valuable diagnostic of the interstellar medium, but uncertainties in reaction rates and branching ratios of reactions involving these ions limit the reliability of conclusions drawn from observations.
AI.method: Isomer-resolved ion-molecule reaction experiments in a cryogenic ion trap, measuring rate coefficients for HOC+ isomerization with H2 and CO, and for threeisomer-producing reactions: CO+ + H2, H3+ + CO, and ArH+ + CO; results were fed into a state-of-the-art astrochemical model.
AI.result: CO+ + H2 predominantly yields HCO+ with negligible HOC+, agreeing with recent theory but strongly contradicting the previously accepted branching ratio; HOC+ isomerizes efficiently to HCO+ with both H2 and CO; the new coefficients measurably affect the predicted HCO+/HOC+ abundance ratio.
AI.conclusion: Isomer-resolved laboratory data substantially revise branching ratios and rates, demonstrating that prior branching assumptions are unreliable and that the new measurements impact astrochemical predictions of the HCO+/HOC+ ratio.

title: A precessing AGN with S-shaped morphology discovered in MALS
comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: We present J1221$-$1354, a precessing AGN discovered in the MeerKAT Absorption Line Survey (MALS) using deep L-band (0.9--1.6\,GHz) radio data. Its `S'-shaped morphology, revealed by the excellent surface brightness sensitivity of MeerKAT, is consistent with jet precession. Ancillary optical and infrared data establish the source as a Type 2 AGN in a moderately overdense environment. The approaching (southern) jet is brighter but shorter than the receding jet, with the northern edge of the receding jet showing a significantly younger spectral age. These features are peculiar, but consistent with a jet reorientation event in an asymmetric ambient medium, in which the jet re-enters a cavity of previously deposited plasma. A simple ballistic model yields a precession period of $P=290\pm30$\,Myr, consistent with geodetic precession in a supermassive black hole binary (SMBHB) with a binary separation of less than 1.1\,pc. We expect that deep radio continuum surveys in the near future will uncover many more such systems, helping to further strengthen the connection between jet precession and SMBHBs, and the latter's implications for the gravitational-wave background detected with pulsar timing arrays.

AI.tldr: J1221$-$1354 is a precessing AGN discovered in MALS with MeerKAT, showing an S-shaped jet consistent with SMBHB-driven geodetic precession (P = 290 ± 30 Myr, separation < 1.1 pc).
AI.motivation: Jet precession is a predicted signature of supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs), which are linked to the nanohertz gravitational-wave background detected by pulsar timing arrays. The authors aim to identify and characterize such precessing systems to strengthen the connection between jet precession and SMBHBs.
AI.method: Discovery and analysis of J1221$-$1354 using deep MeerKAT L-band (0.9–1.6 GHz) radio continuum data from MALS, exploiting high surface brightness sensitivity to reveal the S-shaped morphology. Ancillary optical/IR data classify the source as a Type 2 AGN in a moderately overdense environment. Spectral ageing analysis of the jet lobes and fitting of a simple ballistic precession model are used to derive the precession period and infer binary parameters.
AI.result: The source exhibits an S-shaped morphology consistent with jet precession. The approaching (southern) jet is brighter but shorter than the receding jet, and the northern edge of the receding jet shows a significantly younger spectral age. These features are interpreted as a jet reorientation event in an asymmetric ambient medium where the jet re-enters a cavity of previously deposited plasma. The ballistic model yields a precession period of P = 290 ± 30 Myr, consistent with geodetic precession from an SMBHB with separation < 1.1 pc.
AI.conclusion: J1221$-$1354 is a compelling precessing AGN candidate consistent with an SMBHB. The authors expect future deep radio continuum surveys to uncover many more such systems, further strengthening the link between jet precession and SMBHBs and their implications for the pulsar-timing-array gravitational-wave background.
